sanskrit: tasyālayavariṣṭhasya madhye vipulam āyatam dadarśa bhavanaśreṣṭhaṃ hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ
english: In the midst of that most excellent abode, vast and spacious, Hanumān, the son of the wind-god, beheld the finest of mansions.

sanskrit: ardhayojanavistīrṇam āyataṃ yojanaṃ hi tat bhavanaṃ rākṣasendrasya bahuprāsādasaṃkulam
english: That palace of the lord of rākṣasas was half a yojana in breadth and a full yojana in length, crowded with many turrets.

sanskrit: mārgamāṇas tu vaidehīṃ sītām āyatalocanām sarvataḥ paricakrāma hanūmān arisūdanaḥ
english: Seeking Vaidehī Sītā of the large eyes, Hanumān the destroyer of enemies wandered in every direction.

sanskrit: caturviṣāṇair dviradais triviṣāṇais tathaiva ca parikṣiptam asaṃbādhaṃ rakṣyamāṇam udāyudhaiḥ
english: It was surrounded without obstruction by elephants bearing four tusks and likewise by those bearing three tusks, and guarded by soldiers with upraised weapons.

sanskrit: rākṣasībhiś ca patnībhī rāvaṇasya niveśanam āhṛtābhiś ca vikramya rājakanyābhir āvṛtam
english: The dwelling of Rāvaṇa was enclosed by his rākṣasī wives and by princesses who had been carried off by force.

sanskrit: tan nakramakarākīrṇaṃ timiṃgilajhaṣākulam vāyuvegasamādhūtaṃ pannagair iva sāgaram
english: It teemed with crocodiles and sea-monsters, was filled with timiṅgila fish, and was stirred by the speed of the wind — like the ocean teeming with serpents.

sanskrit: yā hi vaiśvaraṇe lakṣmīr yā cendre harivāhane sā rāvaṇagṛhe sarvā nityam evānapāyinī
english: Whatever wealth and splendor belong to Vaiśravaṇa and to Indra who rides the bay horses — all that was permanently and unfailingly present in Rāvaṇa's abode.

sanskrit: yā ca rājñaḥ kuberasya yamasya varuṇasya ca tādṛśī tad viśiṣṭā vā ṛddhī rakṣo gṛheṣv iha
english: Such prosperity as belongs to King Kubera, to Yama, and to Varuṇa — or even surpassing that — was present here in the dwellings of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tasya harmyasya madhyasthaṃ veśma cānyat sunirmitam bahuniryūha saṃkīrṇaṃ dadarśa pavanātmajaḥ
english: Standing in the midst of that palace, the son of the wind-god saw another exquisitely constructed mansion, dense with many projecting balconies.

sanskrit: brahmaṇo 'rthe kṛtaṃ divyaṃ divi yad viśvakarmaṇā vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ nāma sarvaratnavibhūṣitam
english: In heaven, made by Viśvakarman at the behest of Brahmā, stood the divine aerial car called Puṣpaka, adorned with every kind of jewel.

sanskrit: pareṇa tapasā lebhe yat kuberaḥ pitāmahāt kuberam ojasā jitvā lebhe tad rākṣaseśvaraḥ
english: That which Kubera had obtained from the Grandfather Brahmā through supreme austerity — that very thing the lord of rākṣasas had obtained by vanquishing Kubera by force.

sanskrit: īhā mṛgasamāyuktaiḥ kāryasvarahiraṇmayaiḥ sukṛtair ācitaṃ stambhaiḥ pradīptam iva ca śriyā
english: It was filled with golden pillars fashioned with longing-deer designs, worked in gold of fitting note, and blazed as if ablaze with radiance.

sanskrit: merumandarasaṃkāśair ullikhadbhir ivāmbaram kūṭāgāraiḥ śubhākāraiḥ sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtam
english: It was adorned on all sides with peaked chambers of beautiful form, resembling Meru and Mandara, scratching the sky as it were.

sanskrit: jvalanārkapratīkāśaṃ sukṛtaṃ viśvakarmaṇā hemasopānasaṃyuktaṃ cārupravaravedikam
english: Wrought by Viśvakarman, it shone like blazing sun, furnished with golden stairways and graceful, excellent terraces.

sanskrit: jālavātāyanair yuktaṃ kāñcanaiḥ sthāṭikair api indranīlamahānīlamaṇipravaravedikam vimānaṃ puṣpakaṃ divyam āruroha mahākapiḥ
english: Fitted with latticed windows, of gold and crystal, with terraces of indranīla and mahānīla gems — the great monkey mounted the divine aerial car Puṣpaka.

sanskrit: tatrasthaḥ sa tadā gandhaṃ pānabhakṣyānnasaṃbhavam divyaṃ saṃmūrchitaṃ jighran rūpavantam ivānilam
english: Standing there, he inhaled a divine fragrance arising from drink, food, and cooked dishes — concentrated, like a wind that had taken form.

sanskrit: sa gandhas taṃ mahāsattvaṃ bandhur bandhum ivottamam ita ehīty uvāceva tatra yatra sa rāvaṇaḥ
english: That fragrance drew the mighty-souled one as if a kinsman summoning a kinsman — "Come here" — toward the very place where Rāvaṇa was.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ prasthitaḥ śālāṃ dadarśa mahatīṃ śubhām rāvaṇasya manaḥkāntāṃ kāntām iva varastriyam
english: Then, proceeding in that direction, he saw a great and beautiful hall — beloved of Rāvaṇa's heart, like a lovely noble woman.

sanskrit: maṇisopānavikṛtāṃ hemajālavirājitām sphāṭikair āvṛtatalāṃ dantāntaritarūpikām
english: It was adorned with steps of jewels, brilliant with a lattice of gold, its floor sheathed in crystal, its panels inlaid with ivory.

sanskrit: muktābhiś ca pravālaiś ca rūpyacāmīkarair api vibhūṣitāṃ maṇistambhaiḥ subahustambhabhūṣitām
english: It was embellished with pearls and coral, with silver and gold, and graced with a great multitude of gem-studded pillars.

sanskrit: samair ṛjubhir atyuccaiḥ samantāt suvibhūṣitaiḥ stambhaiḥ pakṣair ivātyuccair divaṃ saṃprasthitām iva
english: With even, straight, exceedingly tall and well-adorned pillars on all sides, like immensely lofty wings, it seemed to be setting out for heaven.

sanskrit: mahatyā kuthayāstrīṇaṃ pṛthivīlakṣaṇāṅkayā pṛthivīm iva vistīrṇāṃ sarāṣṭragṛhamālinīm
english: With a great carpet bearing auspicious earthly marks, it was as vast as the earth itself, garlanded with all the kingdoms and their houses.

sanskrit: nāditāṃ mattavihagair divyagandhādhivāsitām parārdhyāstaraṇopetāṃ rakṣo'dhipaniṣevitām
english: Resounding with intoxicated birds, pervaded by divine fragrances, furnished with the most excellent couches, and frequented by the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: dhūmrām agarudhūpena vimalāṃ haṃsapāṇḍurām citrāṃ puṣpopahāreṇa kalmāṣīm iva suprabhām
english: Smoky with agaru incense, spotless and white as a swan, variegated with offerings of flowers — gleaming like a dappled creature.

sanskrit: manaḥsaṃhlādajananīṃ varṇasyāpi prasādinīm tāṃ śokanāśinīṃ divyāṃ śriyaḥ saṃjananīm iva
english: She who was a delight to the mind, who gladdens even one's complexion, that divine hall that destroys sorrow — like the very birthplace of Śrī.

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthais tu pañca pañcabhir uttamaiḥ tarpayām āsa māteva tadā rāvaṇapālitā
english: The five senses were then gratified by the five excellent sense-objects in that place governed by Rāvaṇa — like a mother gratifying her children.

sanskrit: svargo 'yaṃ devaloko 'yam indrasyeyaṃ purī bhavet siddhir veyaṃ parā hi syād ity amanyata mārutiḥ
english: "Is this heaven? Is this the world of the gods? Could this be Indra's city? Or might this be the highest perfection?" — so Māruti reflected.

sanskrit: pradhyāyata ivāpaśyat pradīpāṃs tatra kāñcanān dhūrtān iva mahādhūrtair devanena parājitān
english: As if lost in thought, he saw the golden lamps there — like cheats defeated by great cheats at gambling.

sanskrit: dīpānāṃ ca prakāśena tejasā rāvaṇasya ca arcirbhir bhūṣaṇānāṃ ca pradīptety abhyamanyata
english: By the radiance of the lamps, the splendor of Rāvaṇa, and the flames of the ornaments — it appeared to be ablaze, so he thought.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyat kuthāsīnaṃ nānāvarṇāmbarasrajam sahasraṃ varanārīṇāṃ nānāveṣavibhūṣitam
english: Then he saw resting on couches a thousand noble women — wearing garments and garlands of many hues, adorned in varied attire.

sanskrit: parivṛtte 'rdharātre tu pānanidrāvaśaṃ gatam krīḍitvoparataṃ rātrau suṣvāpa balavat tadā
english: When midnight had come round, having fallen under the sway of wine-sleep, having ceased from sport during the night, he slept deeply.

sanskrit: tat prasuptaṃ viruruce niḥśabdāntarabhūṣaṇam niḥśabdahaṃsabhramaraṃ yathā padmavanaṃ mahat
english: That assembly sleeping — with ornaments stilled, with geese and bees hushed — shone like a great lotus pond at night.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ saṃvṛtadantāni mīlitākṣāṇi mārutiḥ apaśyat padmagandhīni vadanāni suyoṣitām
english: The son of the wind saw the faces of those lovely women — teeth hidden, eyes closed, fragrant as lotuses.

sanskrit: prabuddhānīva padmāni tāsāṃ bhūtvā kṣapākṣaye punaḥsaṃvṛtapatrāṇi rātrāv iva babhus tadā
english: Like lotuses that had bloomed at the end of darkness and then closed their petals again, so they appeared that night.

sanskrit: imāni mukhapadmāni niyataṃ mattaṣaṭpadāḥ ambujānīva phullāni prārthayanti punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Surely the intoxicated bees must seek these lotus-faces again and again, just as they seek blooming water-lilies."

sanskrit: iti vāmanyata śrīmān upapattyā mahākapiḥ mene hi guṇatas tāni samāni salilodbhavaiḥ
english: So the glorious great monkey reflected by way of analogy — for he judged them equal in quality to water-born lotuses.

sanskrit: sā tasya śuśubhe śālā tābhiḥ strībhir virājitā śāradīva prasannā dyaus tārābhir abhiśobhitā
english: That hall, graced by those women, shone like the clear autumnal sky adorned with stars.

sanskrit: sa ca tābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ śuśubhe rākṣasādhipaḥ yathā hy uḍupatiḥ śrīmāṃs tārābhir abhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: And the lord of rākṣasas, surrounded by them, shone just as the glorious lord of the constellations is surrounded by stars.

sanskrit: yāś cyavante 'mbarāt tārāḥ puṇyaśeṣasamāvṛtāḥ imās tāḥ saṃgatāḥ kṛtsnā iti mene haris tadā
english: "These here must be all those stars that have fallen from the sky, enveloped in the remnant of their merit, gathered together" — so the monkey thought then.

sanskrit: tārāṇām iva suvyaktaṃ mahatīnāṃ śubhārciṣām prabhāvarṇaprasādāś ca virejus tatra yoṣitām
english: Indeed like the great stars of auspicious radiance, the women there shone in the clarity of their luster and complexion.

sanskrit: vyāvṛttagurupīnasrakprakīrṇavarabhūṣaṇāḥ pānavyāyāmakāleṣu nidrāpahṛtacetasaḥ
english: Their heavy and full garlands had slipped aside, their fine ornaments were scattered, their senses carried away by sleep during hours of drinking and exertion.

sanskrit: vyāvṛttatilakāḥ kāś cit kāś cid udbhrāntanūpurāḥ pārśve galitahārāś ca kāś cit paramayoṣitaḥ
english: Some had their brow-marks displaced, some had their anklets fallen awry, some had their pearl-necklaces slipped to the side — those most excellent women.

sanskrit: mukhā hāravṛtāś cānyāḥ kāś cit prasrastavāsasaḥ vyāviddharaśanā dāmāḥ kiśorya iva vāhitāḥ
english: Others had their faces wrapped in garlands; some had their garments slipped; their girdle-strings loosened — like fillies being led away.

sanskrit: sukuṇḍaladharāś cānyā vicchinnamṛditasrajaḥ gajendramṛditāḥ phullā latā iva mahāvane
english: Others wore lovely earrings, their garlands crushed and broken — like flowering creepers in a great forest, trampled by a lordly elephant.

sanskrit: candrāṃśukiraṇābhāś ca hārāś kāsāṃ cid utkaṭāḥ haṃsā iva babhuḥ suptāḥ stanamadhyeṣu yoṣitām
english: The brilliant necklaces of some women, shining like moonbeams, lay between their breasts like sleeping swans.

sanskrit: aparāsāṃ ca vaidūryāḥ kādambā iva pakṣiṇaḥ hemasūtrāṇi cānyāsāṃ cakravākā ivābhavan
english: The vaidūrya gems of others appeared like kādamba birds; the golden threads of still others appeared like cakravāka geese.

sanskrit: haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇāś cakravākopaśobhitāḥ āpagā iva tā rejur jaghanaiḥ pulinair iva
english: Filled with geese and kāraṇḍava ducks and adorned with cakravāka birds, they glittered like rivers — their hips like sandbanks.

sanskrit: kiṅkiṇījālasaṃkāśās tā hemavipulāmbujāḥ bhāvagrāhā yaśastīrāḥ suptā nadya ivābabhuḥ
english: With nets of small bells like lotuses in broad gold, responsive to feeling, renowned as their banks — they lay like sleeping rivers.

sanskrit: mṛduṣv aṅgeṣu kāsāṃ cit kucāgreṣu ca saṃsthitāḥ babhūvur bhūṣaṇānīva śubhā bhūṣaṇarājayaḥ
english: On the soft limbs of some, and resting on the tips of their breasts, the lovely rows of ornaments themselves seemed to be ornaments.

sanskrit: aṃśukāntāś ca kāsāṃ cin mukhamārutakampitāḥ upary upari vaktrāṇāṃ vyādhūyante punaḥ punaḥ
english: The fine garment-ends of some, blown by the breath from their mouths, waved again and again over their faces.

sanskrit: tāḥ pātākā ivoddhūtāḥ patnīnāṃ ruciraprabhāḥ nānāvarṇasuvarṇānāṃ vaktramūleṣu rejire
english: Those cloth-ends, like flags raised aloft, shining with beautiful radiance at the base of the wives' faces, gleamed in the many colors of gold.

sanskrit: vavalguś cātra kāsāṃ cit kuṇḍalāni śubhārciṣām mukhamārutasaṃsargān mandaṃ mandaṃ suyoṣitām
english: The earrings of some of those lovely women, touched by the breath from their mouths, swayed softly, softly, their light auspicious.

sanskrit: śarkarāsavagandhaḥ sa prakṛtyā surabhiḥ sukhaḥ tāsāṃ vadananiḥśvāsaḥ siṣeve rāvaṇaṃ tadā
english: The breath from their mouths — naturally fragrant and sweet, with the scent of sugarcane-liquor — attended on Rāvaṇa then.

sanskrit: rāvaṇānanaśaṅkāś ca kāś cid rāvaṇayoṣitaḥ mukhāni sma sapatnīnām upājighran punaḥ punaḥ
english: And some of Rāvaṇa's wives, mistaking them for Rāvaṇa's face, kissed the faces of their co-wives again and again.

sanskrit: atyarthaṃ saktamanaso rāvaṇe tā varastriyaḥ asvatantrāḥ sapatnīnāṃ priyam evācaraṃs tadā
english: Those noble women, their minds utterly devoted to Rāvaṇa, without independence, acted even toward their co-wives as if doing what was dear to him.

sanskrit: bāhūn upanidhāyānyāḥ pārihārya vibhūṣitāḥ aṃśukāni ca ramyāṇi pramadās tatra śiśyire
english: Placing their arms as pillows, adorned with their ornaments, and lovely garments about them, the women lay there sleeping.

sanskrit: anyā vakṣasi cānyasyās tasyāḥ kā cit punar bhujam aparā tv aṅkam anyasyās tasyāś cāpy aparā bhujau
english: One lay upon another's breast; another upon her arm; still another upon that one's lap; yet another upon her two arms.

sanskrit: ūrupārśvakaṭīpṛṣṭham anyonyasya samāśritāḥ parasparaniviṣṭāṅgyo madasnehavaśānugāḥ
english: Leaning on each other's thighs, flanks, hips, and backs, their bodies interlocked with each other's, led on by the influence of intoxication and love.

sanskrit: anyonyasyāṅgasaṃsparśāt prīyamāṇāḥ sumadhyamāḥ ekīkṛtabhujāḥ sarvāḥ suṣupus tatra yoṣitaḥ
english: Delighting in the mutual touch of their limbs, the slender-waisted women all slept there, their arms merged into one.

sanskrit: anyonyabhujasūtreṇa strīmālāgrathitā hi sā māleva grathitā sūtre śuśubhe mattaṣaṭpadā
english: Strung together by the cord of each other's arms, that garland of women was like a garland threaded on a string, adorned with intoxicated bees.

sanskrit: latānāṃ mādhave māsi phullānāṃ vāyusevanāt anyonyamālāgrathitaṃ saṃsaktakusumoccayam
english: Like creepers in the month of Mādhava blooming and fanned by the wind — their flower clusters clinging together, interwoven in mutual garlands.

sanskrit: vyativeṣṭitasuskantham anyonyabhramarākulam āsīd vanam ivoddhūtaṃ strīvanaṃ rāvaṇasya tat
english: With necks closely entwined, stirred by bees seeking one another, Rāvaṇa's grove of women was like a forest swaying in the wind.

sanskrit: uciteṣv api suvyaktaṃ na tāsāṃ yoṣitāṃ tadā vivekaḥ śakya ādhātuṃ bhūṣaṇāṅgāmbarasrajām
english: Even among those who were used to such things, it was clearly not possible to make any distinction among the women's ornaments, bodies, garments, and garlands.

sanskrit: rāvaṇe sukhasaṃviṣṭe tāḥ striyo vividhaprabhāḥ jvalantaḥ kāñcanā dīpāḥ prekṣantānimiṣā iva
english: With Rāvaṇa comfortably asleep, those women of varied radiance — and the blazing golden lamps — seemed to gaze upon him without blinking.

sanskrit: rājarṣipitṛdaityānāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ ca yoṣitaḥ rakṣasāṃ cābhavan kanyās tasya kāmavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: The daughters of royal sages, of manes, of daityas, of gandharvas, and of rākṣasas had all come under his power of desire.

sanskrit: na tatra kā cit pramadā prasahya vīryopapannena guṇena labdhā na cānyakāmāpi na cānyapūrvā vinā varārhāṃ janakātmajāṃ tu
english: Not one woman there had been won by force — all had been obtained by valor and virtue; none longed for another man, nor had been previously another's — save for Janaka's daughter, who was worthy of the most excellent.

sanskrit: na cākulīnā na ca hīnarūpā nādakṣiṇā nānupacāra yuktā bhāryābhavat tasya na hīnasattvā na cāpi kāntasya na kāmanīyā
english: None was of low birth, none of inferior beauty, none lacking in accomplishments, none without proper conduct; none became his wife who was deficient in virtue, or who was not beloved, or who was not desirable.

sanskrit: babhūva buddhis tu harīśvarasya yadīdṛśī rāghavadharmapatnī imā yathā rākṣasarājabhāryāḥ sujātam asyeti hi sādhubuddheḥ
english: Then the thought arose in the lord of monkeys: "If the lawfully wedded wife of Rāghava were like these wives of the rākṣasa king — how well-born this Rāvaṇa must be!" — for so a good-natured man thinks.

sanskrit: punaś ca so 'cintayad ārtarūpo dhruvaṃ viśiṣṭā guṇato hi sītā athāyam asyāṃ kṛtavān mahātmā laṅkeśvaraḥ kaṣṭam anāryakarma
english: And then he reflected again in anguish: "Surely Sītā must exceed these in virtue; and yet this great-souled lord of Laṅkā has done a cruel, ignoble deed against her."

sanskrit: tatra divyopamaṃ mukhyaṃ sphāṭikaṃ ratnabhūṣitam avekṣamāṇo hanumān dadarśa śayanāsanam
english: There, looking about, Hanumān saw a foremost couch divine in appearance, made of crystal and adorned with jewels.

sanskrit: tasya caikatame deśe so 'gryamālyavibhūṣitam dadarśa pāṇḍuraṃ chatraṃ tārādhipatisaṃnibham
english: In one part of it he saw a white canopy adorned with the finest garlands, resembling the lord of the stars.

sanskrit: bālavyajanahastābhir vījyamānaṃ samantataḥ gandhaiś ca vividhair juṣṭaṃ varadhūpena dhūpitam
english: It was being fanned on all sides by women holding yak-tail fly-whisks; pervaded by various fragrances; fumigated with excellent incense.

sanskrit: paramāstaraṇāstīrṇam āvikājinasaṃvṛtam dāmabhir varamālyānāṃ samantād upaśobhitam
english: Spread with a most excellent coverlet, covered with woolen cloth and skins, beautified on all sides with strings of the finest garlands.

sanskrit: tasmiñ jīmūtasaṃkāśaṃ pradīptottamakuṇḍalam lohitākṣaṃ mahābāhuṃ mahārajatavāsasaṃ
english: Upon it lay one like a rain-cloud in hue, with brilliant, excellent earrings, red-eyed, long-armed, wearing garments of great silver.

sanskrit: lohitenānuliptāṅgaṃ candanena sugandhinā saṃdhyāraktam ivākāśe toyadaṃ sataḍidguṇam
english: His limbs anointed with red sandalpaste of sweet fragrance — like a rain-cloud in the sky reddened at twilight, set with rows of lightning.

sanskrit: vṛtam ābharaṇair divyaiḥ surūpaṃ kāmarūpiṇam savṛkṣavanagulmāḍhyaṃ prasuptam iva mandaram
english: Encircled by divine ornaments, handsome, able to take on any form — like Mount Mandara asleep, abundant with trees, forests, and shrubs.

sanskrit: krīḍitvoparataṃ rātrau varābharaṇabhūṣitam priyaṃ rākṣasakanyānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ sukhāvaham
english: Having ceased from sport during the night, adorned with excellent ornaments, dear to the rākṣasa maidens, the cause of delight to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: pītvāpy uparataṃ cāpi dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ bhāskare śayane vīraṃ prasuptaṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: The great monkey saw that hero, the lord of rākṣasas — having drunk and then ceased — sleeping on a couch that glowed like the sun.

sanskrit: niḥśvasantaṃ yathā nāgaṃ rāvaṇaṃ vānarottamaḥ āsādya paramodvignaḥ so 'pāsarpat subhītavat
english: Approaching Rāvaṇa as he breathed like a serpent, the best of monkeys was greatly agitated and drew back as if in great fear.

sanskrit: athārohaṇam āsādya vedikāntaram āśritaḥ suptaṃ rākṣasaśārdūlaṃ prekṣate sma mahākapiḥ
english: Then, approaching the ascent and taking shelter at the edge of a terrace, the great monkey observed the sleeping tiger among rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śuśubhe rākṣasendrasya svapataḥ śayanottamam gandhahastini saṃviṣṭe yathāprasravaṃ mahat
english: The excellent couch of the lord of rākṣasas as he slept shone like a great spring when a rutting elephant has settled in it.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadanaddhau ca dadarśa sa mahātmanaḥ vikṣiptau rākṣasendrasya bhujāv indradhvajopamau
english: He saw the two outstretched arms of that great-souled lord of rākṣasas, bound with golden armlets, comparable to Indra's banner-poles.

sanskrit: airāvataviṣāṇāgrair āpīḍitakṛtavraṇau vajrollikhitapīnāṃsau viṣṇucakraparikṣitau
english: They bore wounds inflicted by the tusk-tips of Airāvata; their broad shoulders were gashed by Vajra's bolt; they had been struck by Viṣṇu's discus.

sanskrit: pīnau samasujātāṃsau saṃgatau balasaṃyutau sulakṣaṇa nakhāṅguṣṭhau svaṅgulītalalakṣitau
english: Thick, evenly and well-formed at the shoulders, joined together, endowed with strength, their thumbs and nails well-marked with auspicious signs, the palms and fingers bearing good marks.

sanskrit: saṃhatau parighākārau vṛttau karikaropamau vikṣiptau śayane śubhre pañcaśīrṣāv ivoragau
english: Firm, shaped like iron bars, rounded, comparable to elephant's trunks — flung out on the bright couch like two five-headed serpents.

sanskrit: śaśakṣatajakalpena suśītena sugandhinā candanena parārdhyena svanuliptau svalaṃkṛtau
english: Well-anointed and well-adorned with the most excellent sandalwood paste — like fresh blood — cool and fragrant.

sanskrit: uttamastrīvimṛditau gandhottamaniṣevitau yakṣapannagagandharvadevadānavarāviṇau
english: Caressed by the finest women, attended by the best of fragrances, resounding with yakṣas, serpents, gandharvas, gods, and dānavas.

sanskrit: dadarśa sa kapis tasya bāhū śayanasaṃsthitau mandarasyāntare suptau mahārhī ruṣitāv iva
english: The monkey saw those two arms of his, laid on the couch — like two great serpents sleeping in the caverns of Mandara, as if in anger.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ sa paripūrṇābhyāṃ bhujābhyāṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ śuśubhe 'calasaṃkāśaḥ śṛṅgābhyām iva mandaraḥ
english: With those two full arms, the lord of rākṣasas shone like a mountain — like Mandara with its two peaks.

sanskrit: cūtapuṃnāgasurabhir bakulottamasaṃyutaḥ mṛṣṭānnarasasaṃyuktaḥ pānagandhapuraḥsaraḥ
english: Fragrant with mango and puṃnāga trees, mingled with the finest bakula flowers, joined with the juice of fine food, preceded by the scent of drink.

sanskrit: tasya rākṣasasiṃhasya niścakrāma mukhān mahān śayānasya viniḥśvāsaḥ pūrayann iva tad gṛham
english: From the mouth of that lion among rākṣasas as he lay sleeping issued a mighty breath — as if filling that entire dwelling.

sanskrit: muktāmaṇivicitreṇa kāñcanena virājatā mukuṭenāpavṛttena kuṇḍalojjvalitānanam
english: His face was lit by his earrings, his crown — dazzling gold variegated with pearl-jewels — having slipped to one side.

sanskrit: raktacandanadigdhena tathā hāreṇa śobhitā pīnāyataviśālena vakṣasābhivirājitam
english: And adorned with a necklace anointed with red sandalwood, brilliant with his full, long, and broad chest.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇāpaviddhena kṣaumeṇa kṣatajekṣaṇam mahārheṇa susaṃvītaṃ pītenottamavāsasā
english: His eyes blood-red, a white silk cloth flung aside, neatly wrapped in yellow, most excellent upper garments.

sanskrit: māṣarāśipratīkāśaṃ niḥśvasantaṃ bhujaṅgavat gāṅge mahati toyānte prasutamiva kuñjaram
english: Dark as a heap of black beans, breathing like a serpent — like an elephant plunged into the great Gaṅgā's deep water.

sanskrit: caturbhiḥ kāñcanair dīpair dīpyamānaiś caturdiśam prakāśīkṛtasarvāṅgaṃ meghaṃ vidyudgaṇair iva
english: Illuminated in all four directions by four blazing golden lamps, his entire body made bright — like a cloud surrounded by masses of lightning.

sanskrit: pādamūlagatāś cāpi dadarśa sumahātmanaḥ patnīḥ sa priyabhāryasya tasya rakṣaḥpater gṛhe
english: And at his feet he saw the wives of that most great-souled one, who was fond of his wives, in the house of that lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: śaśiprakāśavadanā varakuṇḍalabhūṣitāḥ amlānamālyābharaṇā dadarśa hariyūthapaḥ
english: Faces shining like the moon, adorned with excellent earrings, their garlands and ornaments unfaded — so the lord of the monkey-troop saw them.

sanskrit: nṛttavāditrakuśalā rākṣasendrabhujāṅkagāḥ varābharaṇadhāriṇyo niṣannā dadṛśe kapiḥ
english: Skilled in dancing and playing instruments, resting in the embrace of the lord of rākṣasas, wearing excellent ornaments — the monkey saw them seated.

sanskrit: vajravaidūryagarbhāṇi śravaṇānteṣu yoṣitām dadarśa tāpanīyāni kuṇḍalāny aṅgadāni ca
english: At the ears of the women he saw earrings and armlets of refined gold, set with diamonds and vaidūrya gems.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ candropamair vaktraiḥ śubhair lalitakuṇḍalaiḥ virarāja vimānaṃ tan nabhas tārāgaṇair iva
english: With their moon-like faces and beautiful, graceful earrings, that aerial palace shone like the sky adorned with multitudes of stars.

sanskrit: madavyāyāmakhinnās tā rākṣasendrasya yoṣitaḥ teṣu teṣv avakāśeṣu prasuptās tanumadhyamāḥ
english: Wearied by intoxication and exertion, the slender-waisted wives of the lord of rākṣasas lay sleeping in various spaces.

sanskrit: kā cid vīṇāṃ pariṣvajya prasuptā saṃprakāśate mahānadīprakīrṇeva nalinī potam āśritā
english: One, embracing a vīṇā and asleep, appeared bright — like a lotus plant in a great river, clinging to a young sprout.

sanskrit: anyā kakṣagatenaiva maḍḍukenāsitekṣaṇā prasuptā bhāminī bhāti bālaputreva vatsalā
english: Another dark-eyed woman, with a small drum at her side, lay sleeping and shone like a fond mother with her young child.

sanskrit: paṭahaṃ cārusarvāṅgī pīḍya śete śubhastanī cirasya ramaṇaṃ labdhvā pariṣvajyeva kāminī
english: One of beautiful limbs and auspicious breasts lay pressing a kettledrum — like a passionate woman embracing a long-desired lover.

sanskrit: kā cid aṃśaṃ pariṣvajya suptā kamalalocanā nidrāvaśam anuprāptā sahakānteva bhāminī
english: One lotus-eyed woman lay asleep, embracing a drum-stand, having fallen under the power of sleep — like a beauty with her beloved.

sanskrit: anyā kanakasaṃkāśair mṛdupīnair manoramaiḥ mṛdaṅgaṃ paripīḍyāṅgaiḥ prasuptā mattalocanā
english: Another, with intoxicated eyes, pressed a mṛdaṅga drum with her soft, full, beautiful limbs shining like gold, and lay asleep.

sanskrit: bhujapārśvāntarasthena kakṣageṇa kṛśodarī paṇavena sahānindyā suptā madakṛtaśramā
english: A slender-waisted, blameless woman lay asleep, wearied by intoxication, a small drum resting between her arm and side.

sanskrit: ḍiṇḍimaṃ parigṛhyānyā tathaivāsaktaḍiṇḍimā prasuptā taruṇaṃ vatsam upagūhyeva bhāminī
english: Another, having grasped a double-drum and still clinging to it, lay asleep — like a beautiful woman embracing a young calf.

sanskrit: kā cid āḍambaraṃ nārī bhujasaṃbhogapīḍitam kṛtvā kamalapatrākṣī prasuptā madamohitā
english: One lotus-petal-eyed woman, having pressed a great drum with her embrace of arms, lay asleep, stupefied by intoxication.

sanskrit: kalaśīm apaviddhyānyā prasuptā bhāti bhāminī vasante puṣpaśabalā māleva parimārjitā
english: Another, having set aside a water-jar, lay asleep and shone — like a garland in spring, streaked with flowers, freshly arranged.

sanskrit: pāṇibhyāṃ ca kucau kā cit suvarṇakalaśopamau upagūhyābalā suptā nidrābalaparājitā
english: One woman lay asleep, overcome by the force of sleep, clasping her breasts — resembling golden water-pots — with both hands.

sanskrit: anyā kamalapatrākṣī pūrṇendusadṛśānanā anyām āliṅgya suśroṇī prasuptā madavihvalā
english: Another, lotus-petal-eyed, her face like the full moon, fine-hipped, lay asleep embracing another woman, bewildered by intoxication.

sanskrit: ātodyāni vicitrāṇi pariṣvajya varastriyaḥ nipīḍya ca kucaiḥ suptāḥ kāminyaḥ kāmukān iva
english: Those noble and amorous women lay asleep embracing various musical instruments and pressing them with their breasts — as if embracing their lovers.

sanskrit: tāsām ekāntavinyaste śayānāṃ śayane śubhe dadarśa rūpasaṃpannām aparāṃ sa kapiḥ striyam
english: Apart from them, lying on an auspicious couch in a secluded place, the monkey saw another woman possessed of great beauty.

sanskrit: muktāmaṇisamāyuktair bhūṣaṇaiḥ suvibhūṣitām vibhūṣayantīm iva ca svaśriyā bhavanottamam
english: Well-adorned with ornaments set with pearls and gems — as if adorning the excellent palace itself with her own radiance.

sanskrit: gaurīṃ kanakavarṇābhām iṣṭām antaḥpureśvarīm kapir mandodarīṃ tatra śayānāṃ cārurūpiṇīm
english: The monkey saw there, lying and lovely in form — fair, golden in hue, beloved, mistress of the inner apartments — Mandodarī.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābāhur bhūṣitāṃ mārutātmajaḥ tarkayām āsa sīteti rūpayauvanasaṃpadā harṣeṇa mahatā yukto nananda hariyūthapaḥ
english: The long-armed son of the wind, seeing her adorned thus, guessed her to be Sītā by her wealth of beauty and youth; filled with great joy, the lord of the monkey-troop rejoiced.

sanskrit: āsphoṭayām āsa cucumba pucchaṃ nananda cikrīḍa jagau jagāma stambhān arohan nipapāta bhūmau nidarśayan svāṃ prakṛtiṃ kapīnām
english: He slapped his arms, kissed his tail, rejoiced, frolicked, sang, went about, climbed the pillars, fell to the ground — displaying the very nature of monkeys.

sanskrit: avadhūya ca tāṃ buddhiṃ babhūvāvasthitas tadā jagāma cāparāṃ cintāṃ sītāṃ prati mahākapiḥ
english: Then shaking off that thought he became still, and the great monkey turned to another reflection concerning Sītā.

sanskrit: na rāmeṇa viyuktā sā svaptum arhati bhāminī na bhoktuṃ nāpy alaṃkartuṃ na pānam upasevitum
english: "That noble woman, separated from Rāma, cannot be sleeping, or eating, or adorning herself, or drinking.

sanskrit: nānyaṃ naram upasthātuṃ surāṇām api ceśvaram na hi rāmasamaḥ kaś cid vidyate tridaśeṣv api anyeyam iti niścitya pānabhūmau cacāra saḥ
english: She cannot be attending on another man, even if he were lord of the gods — for there exists no one equal to Rāma, not even among the thirty gods." Having thus concluded that this was another woman, he wandered through the drinking hall.

sanskrit: krīḍitenāparāḥ klāntā gītena ca tathā parāḥ nṛttena cāparāḥ klāntāḥ pānaviprahatās tathā
english: Some were wearied by play, others by singing; still others were wearied by dancing; others were overwhelmed by drink.

sanskrit: murajeṣu mṛdaṅgeṣu pīṭhikāsu ca saṃsthitāḥ tathāstaraṇamukhyyeṣu saṃviṣṭāś cāparāḥ striyaḥ
english: Some women were lying on muraja-drums, on mṛdaṅgas, and on stools; others had settled onto the finest of couches and spreads.

sanskrit: aṅganānāṃ sahasreṇa bhūṣitena vibhūṣaṇaiḥ rūpasaṃlāpaśīlena yuktagītārthabhāṣiṇā
english: With a thousand women adorned with ornaments, skilled in beauty and conversation, apt in speaking the meaning of songs,

sanskrit: deśakālābhiyuktena yuktavākyābhidhāyinā ratābhiratasaṃsuptaṃ dadarśa hariyūthapaḥ
english: suited to time and place, speaking fitting words — the lord of the monkey-troop saw him sleeping, sated with love after love.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ madhye mahābāhuḥ śuśubhe rākṣaseśvaraḥ goṣṭhe mahati mukhyānāṃ gavāṃ madhye yathā vṛṣaḥ
english: In their midst the long-armed lord of rākṣasas shone — like a bull in a great pen, amid the finest cows.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasendraḥ śuśubhe tābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ svayam kareṇubhir yathāraṇyaṃ parikīrṇo mahādvipaḥ
english: That lord of rākṣasas himself, surrounded by them, shone — like a great elephant in a forest, encircled by she-elephants.

sanskrit: sarvakāmair upetāṃ ca pānabhūmiṃ mahātmanaḥ dadarśa kapiśārdūlas tasya rakṣaḥpater gṛhe
english: The tiger among monkeys saw the drinking hall of that great-souled one, provided with every pleasure, in the house of that lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca varāhāṇāṃ ca bhāgaśaḥ tatra nyastāni māṃsāni pānabhūmau dadarśa saḥ
english: He saw there, in the drinking hall, portions of the flesh of deer, buffalo, and boar laid out.

sanskrit: raukmeṣu ca viśaleṣu bhājaneṣv ardhabhakṣitān dadarśa kapiśārdūla mayūrān kukkuṭāṃs tathā
english: In large golden vessels the tiger among monkeys saw peacocks and cocks, half-eaten.

sanskrit: varāhavārdhrāṇasakān dadhisauvarcalāyutān śalyān mṛgamayūrāṃś ca hanūmān anvavaikṣata
english: Hanumān observed boar and dried-meat preparations mixed with curd and black salt, roasted meats, and flesh of deer and peacock.

sanskrit: kṛkarān vividhān siddhāṃś cakorān ardhabhakṣitān mahiṣān ekaśalyāṃś ca chāgāṃś ca kṛtaniṣṭhitān lekhyam uccāvacaṃ peyaṃ bhojyāni vividhāni ca
english: Various cooked partridges, cakor birds half-eaten, whole-skewered buffalo, and goats well-prepared; lickable items both high and low, drinks, and various foods.

sanskrit: tathāmlalavaṇottaṃsair vividhai rāgaṣāḍavaiḥ hāra nūpurakeyūrair apaviddhair mahādhanaiḥ
english: Along with various sour and salt condiments and colored sweet-and-sour sauces; necklaces, anklets, and armlets of great value strewn about.

sanskrit: pānabhājanavikṣiptaiḥ phalaiś ca vividhair api kṛtapuṣpopahārā bhūr adhikaṃ puṣyati śriyam
english: With drinking vessels scattered about and various fruits as well, and floral offerings made — the floor bloomed with surpassing splendor.

sanskrit: tatra tatra ca vinyastaiḥ suśliṣṭaiḥ śayanāsanaiḥ pānabhūmir vinā vahniṃ pradīptevopalakṣyate
english: With couches and seats well-arranged and placed here and there, the drinking hall appeared to be ablaze even without fire.

sanskrit: bahuprakārair vividhair varasaṃskārasaṃskṛtaiḥ māṃsaiḥ kuśalasaṃyuktaiḥ pānabhūmigataiḥ pṛthak
english: With meats of many varied kinds, prepared with excellent seasoning and skillfully combined, placed separately in the drinking hall.

sanskrit: divyāḥ prasannā vividhāḥ surāḥ kṛtasurā api śarkarāsavamādhvīkāḥ puṣpāsavaphalāsavāḥ vāsacūrṇaiś ca vividhair mṛṣṭās tais taiḥ pṛthakpṛthak
english: Divine, clear, varied wines and distilled spirits as well — sugarcane-spirits, mead, flower-spirits and fruit-spirits — each purified with its particular perfumed powder, separately displayed.

sanskrit: saṃtatā śuśubhe bhūmir mālyaiś ca bahusaṃsthitaiḥ hiraṇmayaiś ca karakair bhājanaiḥ sphāṭikair api jāmbūnadamayaiś cānyaiḥ karakair abhisaṃvṛtā
english: The floor was continuously beautiful with many garlands laid about it, covered over with golden water-vessels, crystal cups, and yet other drinking vessels of Jāmbūnada-gold.

sanskrit: rājateṣu ca kumbheṣu jāmbūnadamayeṣu ca pānaśreṣṭhaṃ tadā bhūri kapis tatra dadarśa ha
english: In silver pitchers and in those of Jāmbūnada-gold, the monkey then and there saw an abundance of the finest drink.

sanskrit: so 'paśyac chātakumbhāni śīdhor maṇimayāni ca rājatāni ca pūrṇāni bhājanāni mahākapiḥ
english: The great monkey saw vessels of pure gold, of jewels, and of silver, all brimming full with fermented liquor.

sanskrit: kva cid ardhāvaśeṣāṇi kva cit pītāni sarvaśaḥ kva cin naiva prapītāni pānāni sa dadarśa ha
english: In some places he saw drinks with half remaining, in others entirely consumed, in still others not yet drunk at all.

sanskrit: kva cid bhakṣyāṃś ca vividhān kva cit pānāni bhāgaśaḥ kva cid annāvaśeṣāṇi paśyan vai vicacāra ha
english: Seeing various eatables in one place, portions of drink in another, and remnants of food in yet another, he wandered about.

sanskrit: kva cit prabhinnaiḥ karakaiḥ kva cid āloḍitair ghaṭaiḥ kva cit saṃpṛktamālyāni jalāni ca phalāni ca
english: In some places with broken drinking cups, in others with overturned pitchers, in yet others water and fruits mixed with garlands.

sanskrit: śayanāny atra nārīṇāṃ śūnyāni bahudhā punaḥ parasparaṃ samāśliṣya kāś cit suptā varāṅganāḥ
english: The women's couches here were empty in many places; some noble women lay sleeping, embracing one another.

sanskrit: kā cic ca vastram anyasyā apahṛtyopaguhya ca upagamyābalā suptā nidrābalaparājitā
english: One woman had taken another's garment, wrapped it around herself and embraced it, and lay sleeping, overcome by the force of sleep.

sanskrit: tāsām ucchvāsavātena vastraṃ mālyaṃ ca gātrajam nātyarthaṃ spandate citraṃ prāpya mandam ivānilam
english: The garments and body-garlands of those women, moved by the breeze of their breathing, stirred gently, like a light wind barely reaching them.

sanskrit: candanasya ca śītasya śīdhor madhurasasya ca vividhasya ca mālyasya puṣpasya vividhasya ca
english: Of cool sandalwood and sweet fermented liquor, of various garlands, and of various flowers —

sanskrit: bahudhā mārutas tatra gandhaṃ vividham udvahan snānānāṃ candanānāṃ ca dhūpānāṃ caiva mūrchitaḥ pravavau surabhir gandho vimāne puṣpake tadā
english: — in that place the wind bore aloft many varied fragrances; made dense with the scents of bathing substances, sandalwoods, and incense, a fragrant perfume blew through the aerial car Puṣpaka then.

sanskrit: śyāmāvadātās tatrānyāḥ kāś cit kṛṣṇā varāṅganāḥ kāś cit kāñcanavarṇāṅgyaḥ pramadā rākṣasālaye
english: Some women there were dark-complexioned and fair; some were wholly dark, those noble ladies; some had limbs of golden hue — those beauties in the rākṣasa dwelling.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ nidrāvaśatvāc ca madanena vimūrchitam padminīnāṃ prasuptānāṃ rūpam āsīd yathaiva hi
english: Indeed, by virtue of their being under the sway of sleep and swooning with love, they had the appearance of sleeping lotus plants.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvam aśeṣeṇa rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṃ kapiḥ dadarśa sumahātejā na dadarśa ca jānakīm
english: Thus the monkey of immense brilliance surveyed the entirety of Rāvaṇa's inner apartments without exception — and yet did not see Jānakī.

sanskrit: nirīkṣamāṇaś ca tatas tāḥ striyaḥ sa mahākapiḥ jagāma mahatīṃ cintāṃ dharmasādhvasaśaṅkitaḥ
english: And then, having looked upon those women, the great monkey fell into deep reflection, troubled by apprehension about his duty.

sanskrit: paradārāvarodhasya prasuptasya nirīkṣaṇam idaṃ khalu mamātyarthaṃ dharmalopaṃ kariṣyati
english: "Surely this act of gazing upon the inner apartments — upon another man's wives while they sleep — will cause me a great violation of dharma.

sanskrit: na hi me paradārāṇāṃ dṛṣṭir viṣayavartinī ayaṃ cātra mayā dṛṣṭaḥ paradāraparigrahaḥ
english: My gaze has not been directed toward another man's wives with sensual intent; and yet what I have seen here is another man's wife's domain.

sanskrit: tasya prādurabhūc cintāpunar anyā manasvinaḥ niścitaikāntacittasya kāryaniścayadarśinī
english: Then another thought arose for that resolute and steadfast one of fixed single mind — a thought that discerned the certainty of the task.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayā sarvā viśvastā rāvaṇastriyaḥ na tu me manasaḥ kiṃ cid vaikṛtyam upapadyate
english: "Though I have indeed seen all of Rāvaṇa's wives with confidence, yet not the slightest perturbation has come upon my mind.

sanskrit: mano hi hetuḥ sarveṣām indriyāṇāṃ pravartane śubhāśubhāsv avasthāsu tac ca me suvyavasthitam
english: For the mind is the cause of all the senses' activity in auspicious and inauspicious conditions — and mine is perfectly controlled.

sanskrit: nānyatra hi mayā śakyā vaidehī parimārgitum striyo hi strīṣu dṛśyante sadā saṃparimārgaṇe
english: For nowhere else could Vaidehī have been sought by me — for women are always to be looked for among women when searching.

sanskrit: yasya sattvasya yā yonis tasyāṃ tat parimārgyate na śakyaṃ pramadā naṣṭā mṛgīṣu parimārgitum
english: A creature is to be sought in its own kind of abode — a lost woman cannot be sought among does.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ mārgitaṃ tāvac chuddhena manasā mayā rāvaṇāntaḥpuraṃ saraṃ dṛśyate na ca jānakī
english: So this has been searched by me with a pure mind — the entire inner apartments of Rāvaṇa are seen, yet Jānakī is not seen.

sanskrit: devagandharvakanyāś ca nāgakanyāś ca vīryavān avekṣamāṇo hanumān naivāpaśyata jānakīm
english: The valiant Hanumān, looking about even among the daughters of gods, gandharvas, and nāga maidens, did not see Jānakī.

sanskrit: tām apaśyan kapis tatra paśyaṃś cānyā varastriyaḥ apakramya tadā vīraḥ pradhyātum upacakrame
english: Not seeing her there, but seeing the other noble women, that heroic monkey withdrew and began to reflect deeply.
